Overview

Update the PayPal plan upgrade process to use the webhook-first workflow, matching the standard subscription flow. Instead of relying on client-side capture requests, upgrades are processed securely via the PayPal webhook with real-time status updates delivered through Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Objectives

  • Save upgrade details upon subscription creation so the webhook has the full upgrade context.
  • Finalize the plan upgrade (cancel previous subscription and activate new plan) directly during webhook processing.
  • Broadcast real-time status updates to the frontend via SSE.
  • Keep the capture endpoint strictly as a safe, idempotent fallback.

issues.display_title: Issue #1951: PayPal Downgrade: align path with SUBSCRIBE (webhook-first + SSE)
issues.main_description_html:
Context & Problem Statement

Previously, PayPal subscription downgrades relied on client-side execution via POST /paypal/subscriptions/capture (DowngradeHandler.php). If a user closes the browser, refreshes, or loses internet connection immediately after approving the revision in PayPal's popup, GoThru's database is never updated, leading to desynchronized subscription states and billing discrepancies.

This task migrates PayPal downgrade orchestration to a resilient Webhook-First pattern, making PayPal webhooks the single source of truth for database mutations, fully aligned with the existing SUBSCRIBE and UPGRADE flows.

Related Frontend Issue: GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4332

Scope of Work & Acceptance Criteria

  • Persist Downgrade Intent (CreateSubscription.php):
    • After a successful PayPal subscription revision call (/v1/billing/subscriptions/{id}/revise), store downgrade intent metadata in Redis Toronto: paypal:sub_intent:{subscriptionId} with a 24-hour TTL.
    • Include user_id, plan, target_plan_code, target_plan_id, and is_photo_studio in the payload.
    • Update Redis binding (PaypalSubscriptionBindingHelper) to map the subscription to the new plan.
  • Process Webhook Events (DowngradeIntentProcessor.php):
    • Route BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.UPDATED and BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.ACTIVATED webhook events in HandlePaypalWebhook.php to DowngradeIntentProcessor.
    • Implement a distributed Redis lock (paypal:sub_downgrade_lock:{subscriptionId}, TTL 120s) to prevent concurrent execution from duplicate webhooks.
    • Enforce attestation checks: subscription status must strictly be ACTIVE, and PayPal plan_id must match target_plan_id.
    • Validate that $subscriptionId matches the user's active recurring_profile to prevent stale intent replay if the user switched to an Upgrade.
  • Database Scheduling & Status Emission:
    • Idempotently schedule the plan downgrade in tableUnsubscribes (unsubscribe_type = '3', effective at next_billing_time).
    • Emit status active (amount: 0.0) to Redis key paypal:sub_status:{subscriptionId} (TTL 1h) for SSE stream consumption, then delete the intent and release lock.
  • Payment Isolation & Idempotent Capture Fallback:
    • Decouple downgrade processing from PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php to prevent swallowing recurring renewal payments and invoices.
    • Maintain legacy DowngradeHandler.php as an idempotent fallback that checks for existing DB entries and returns a clean HTTP 200 OK.

Result

Implementation Proof

  • Pull Request: #1979 (base: main)
  • Commits:
    • a078cbecb (Initial webhook-first downgrade implementation)
    • 3fcefbeae (Hardened security, idempotency, and edge-case handling post-review)
  • Core Files Changed:
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/DowngradeIntentProcessor.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/CreateSubscription.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/HandlePaypalWebhook.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/DowngradeHandler.php

issues.display_title: Issue #1974: fix(invoice): handle missing billing address gracefully during invoice generation
issues.main_description_html:
Description

When a user unlocks a hosted overlay (or goes through any one-time payment / subscription flow triggering invoice generation), a fatal unhandled exception occurred if the user had not previously saved their billing address details.

Root Cause

In InvoiceHelper::generateInvoicePdf() and BillingClass::generateInvoiceV2(), billing information was retrieved using:

$billingInfo = $this->databaseClass->tableBillingAddress()->where('user_id', $userId)->get();
$billingInfo = json_decode(json_encode($billingInfo), true);
$billingInfo = $billingInfo[0];

When no row exists in billing_address for the user, $billingInfo evaluates to an empty array []. Accessing index 0 throws:

ErrorException: Undefined array key 0

Solution

  1. Replaced get() with first() to retrieve a single record cleanly.
  2. Added a graceful fallback: if no billing address record is found, user name (first_name, last_name) and country are retrieved directly from the users table, setting empty string fallbacks for street address, city, state, postal code, and company name.
  3. Added PHPUnit test coverage (InvoiceHelperBillingFallbackTest) simulating users with missing billing address entries.

Result

  • Affected Tour Verified: Tour pziWHtJt (user_id 16127) activated successfully in overlay_audit.

issues.display_title: Issue #1975: feat(auth): support Keycloak Bearer token in Authenticate middleware for external ecosystem apps
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Enable the auth route middleware (App\Http\Middleware\Authenticate) to natively verify and accept standard Keycloak OIDC Access Tokens (Authorization: Bearer <token>). This allows sibling apps in the GoThru ecosystem (such as Panorra, mobile apps, or internal microservices) to call GoThru API endpoints directly using their Keycloak SSO identity without needing custom token-exchange roundtrips or legacy gt. tokens.

Background & Problem

  • Currently, Authenticate.php only accepts legacy internal tokens formatted as gt.<jwt> signed with symmetric HS256 (KEY_TOKEN).
  • External ecosystem products like Panorra authenticate users directly against Keycloak SSO and receive RS256-signed Keycloak access tokens.
  • Sibling apps are currently forced to execute an extra login exchange (POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login) or bypass authentication entirely on certain endpoints.

Proposed Changes

  1. Dual-Driver Token Classifier in Authenticate.php:

    • Inspect the Authorization header.
    • Strip leading Bearer prefix if present.
    • If token begins with gt., route to the existing legacy handler (checkToken / KEY_TOKEN).
    • If token is a Keycloak JWT, route to the Keycloak validation handler.

  2. Keycloak Verification Driver:

    • Verify RS256 signature using the Keycloak realm JWKS endpoint via KeycloakTokenHelper::verifyAndGetClaims() (cached in Redis for 1 hour).
    • Validate realm issuer (KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL/realms/{realm}).
    • Validate authorized party (azp) or audience (aud) against configured KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS.

  3. User Resolution & JIT Provisioning:

    • Lookup existing user by keycloak_sub.
    • Fallback to matching by email and link keycloak_sub to the user record.
    • If user does not exist in GoThru and email_verified === true, JIT provision user profile and defaults via KeycloakUserRegistrar::register().

  4. Request Enrichment (Backward Compatibility):

    • Merge user_id, subscribtion, and user_data into $request so all downstream controllers function without code changes.

  5. Configuration Update:

    • Update KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS in environment configuration to include client identifiers for Panorra (e.g. gothru-dashboard,panorra,panorra-app,app-gothru-local).

  6. Automated Tests:

    • Add unit/feature tests for Authenticate middleware covering valid Keycloak tokens, expired tokens, untrusted clients, missing user cases, and request attribute injection.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Requests bearing a valid Keycloak access token with an allowed client ID (e.g., Panorra) are accepted by all routes protected by middleware => 'auth'.
  • Downstream controllers receive consistent $request->user_id, $request->subscribtion, and $request->user_data.
  • Legacy gt. tokens continue to work identically with zero regression for GoThru Dashboard.
  • Expired, untrusted client, or tampered Keycloak tokens are rejected with HTTP 401.
  • Unit and route tests pass cleanly.

Result

🚀 Implementation Deliverables

  • Pull Request: #1976 (Merged into main).
  • Key Files & Changes:
    • app/Http/Middleware/Authenticate.php: Hybrid dual-driver auth middleware with native Keycloak RS256 Bearer token support alongside legacy gt.<jwt> tokens.
    • app/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakUserResolver.php: Extracted shared user resolution, auto-linking (keycloak_sub), and JIT provisioning helper.
    • app/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelper.php: Added panorra and panorra-app to default allowed Keycloak clients.
    • app/Actions/Auth/KeycloakLoginAction.php: Refactored to delegate user resolution to KeycloakUserResolver.

🔬 Automated Testing & Verification

  • Unit Test Suites:
    • tests/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTest.php: 16/16 tests passed (100%).
    • tests/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakUserResolverTest.php: 7/7 tests passed (100%).
    • tests/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelperTest.php: 7/7 tests passed (100%).
  • Live E2E Verification (verified on protected endpoint /users/detail with user muhamad.rifky.dev@gmail.com / User ID: 50214):
    • Legacy gt.<jwt> token with and without Bearer prefix: 200 OK.
    • Keycloak RS256 Bearer token (panorra & gothru-dashboard clients): 200 OK (auto-linked keycloak_sub).
    • Security negative tests (expired token, unauthorized client, unverified email, account linking conflict, rogue signature): all rejected with 401 Unauthorized.

issues.display_title: Issue #1983: [API Provider] Implement Internal Endpoint GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours with Keycloak Service Auth
issues.main_description_html:
Upstream References

  • Parent Epic: GoThruMedia/gothru-sso#9 (Epic: GoThru App-to-App Data Exchange Integration)
  • Parent Task: GoThruMedia/gothru-sso#12 (Task 3: Implement Provider Capabilities)

1. Overview & Goal

Enable GoThru-API-New to act as a secure Data Provider by exposing an internal endpoint that serves virtual tours from hosted_tours.tours to other GoThru services (such as Panorra Backend, Villume, etc.) on behalf of an authenticated user identified by their Keycloak UUID (keycloak_sub).

The internal route must be protected using OAuth2 Keycloak Service Account tokens (client_credentials) with route-level authorization and idempotent JIT user provisioning.

2. Endpoint Specification

  • HTTP Method & Path:
    • GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours
    • (Alias: GET /v1/internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours)
  • Query Parameters:
    • search (string, optional): Case-insensitive keyword filter matching tour_name or tour_key.
    • page (integer, default: 1): Active page number.
    • per_page (integer, default: 20, max: 100): Number of tour records per page.
  • Headers:
    • Authorization: Bearer <keycloak-service-account-token>
    • Accept: application/json

3. Technical Requirements

A. Keycloak Service Auth Middleware (KeycloakServiceAuthMiddleware)

  1. Extract Bearer token from Authorization header. If missing, return 401 Unauthorized.
  2. Verify RS256 token signature against Keycloak JWKS (cached in local memory/Redis without network calls on hot-path).
  3. Validate claims:
    • iss: matches configured Keycloak realm URL.
    • aud: matches provider API audience contract (gothru-api).
    • exp: token must not be expired (accounting for clock skew).
    • nbf: token must be active.
  4. Verify caller authorization:
    • Extract caller identifier from azp or client_id (e.g. panorra-service, villume-service).
    • Enforce route-aware permission checking (e.g., caller must have gothru.tours.read permission).
    • If caller is not in allowlist or lacks required permission, return 403 Forbidden without touching the database.

B. Request Validation & Identity Resolution

  1. Validate {uuid} parameter against RFC 4122 UUID syntax regex. Return 400 Bad Request if malformed.
  2. Resolve user in database connection gothru_mod, table users by matching keycloak_sub = :uuid.
  3. Idempotent JIT Provisioning:
    • If user does not exist in gothru_mod.users, create a minimal user record linked to keycloak_sub using atomic SQL (INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE) to guarantee concurrency safety.
    • Newly provisioned users immediately yield an empty result ({ data: [], pagination: { total: 0, ... } }).

C. Data Retrieval (hosted_tours.tours)

  1. Query table tours on database connection hosted_tours where user_id = :local_user_id and deactivated = '0'.
  2. Apply search filter if provided: tour_name LIKE %search% OR tour_key LIKE %search%.
  3. Select all schema properties from hosted_tours.tours, explicitly omitting internal user_id for external security.
  4. Order results by creation_date DESC and apply pagination offset/limit.

D. Response Contract

  • 200 OK with JSON envelope { data: [...], pagination: { total, page, per_page, total_pages } }.
  • 200 OK with empty data array { data: [], pagination: { total: 0, ... } } when no tours exist or user is newly JIT-provisioned (MUST NEVER return 404).
  • 400 Bad Request when {uuid} format is invalid.
  • 401 Unauthorized when token is missing, expired, or invalid.
  • 403 Forbidden when caller service is unauthorized or lacks route permission.

4. Planned Deliverables

  • app/Http/Middleware/KeycloakServiceAuthMiddleware.php: Token validation, JWKS caching & allowlist authorization.
  • routes/v1/internal_virtual_tours.php: Dedicated internal route group.
  • bootstrap/app.php: Middleware registration & route inclusion.
  • app/Repositories/Internal/InternalVirtualTourRepository.php: Multi-DB logic, atomic JIT, pagination, keyword search & schema sanitization.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Internal/GetUserVirtualToursInternalController.php: Request validation & query handling.
  • tests/Http/Controllers/Internal/GetUserVirtualToursInternalControllerTest.php: Complete unit & feature tests.

5. Acceptance Criteria

  • Unauthenticated requests return 401 Unauthorized.
  • Authenticated requests from unapproved azp clients return 403 Forbidden.
  • Malformed UUID parameters return 400 Bad Request.
  • Existing users with published tours return 200 OK with JSON envelope and pagination.
  • Existing users with zero tours return 200 OK with { data: [], pagination: { total: 0, ... } }.
  • Unknown valid Keycloak UUIDs are JIT-provisioned in gothru_mod.users and return 200 OK.
  • All unit and feature tests pass cleanly.

issues.display_title: Issue #1987: research(tours): Data research on tour distance calculation and path lengths based on panorama navigation links
issues.main_description_html:
Overview & Goal

Perform data research and feasibility analysis on measuring the real physical distance and path length of virtual tours. The goal is to investigate how to accurately calculate the total distance covered by tours (especially sv_publishing and outdoor tours) using geographical coordinates and actual navigation links, rather than simple sequence order.

Scope of Research

  1. Distance Calculation Methodology:

    • Compare sequence-based traversal (4_panoramas.sequence) vs actual hotspot navigation graph (5_panoramas_links).
    • Identify how branching paths, dead-ends, and loops affect distance metrics.
    • Formulate accurate geodesic distance calculation (Haversine formula) across connected nodes (1_panorama_left $\leftrightarrow$ 2_panorama_right).

  2. Dataset Investigation & Criteria Matching:

    • Sample and analyze real tour datasets in the database.
    • Identify candidate tours with long-distance paths (> 1 km up to multi-kilometer routes).
    • Evaluate data anomalies (e.g. invalid GPS lat/lng, discontinuous jumps, unlinked nodes).

  3. Deliverables:

    • Document calculation logic and edge case considerations.
    • Compile verified list of benchmark tours (> 1 km) with their exact link counts and path lengths.
    • Provide summary data artifact for reference.

Result

issues.display_title: Issue #1988: fix(paypal): Harden PayPal subscription endpoints against DoS, SQL wildcard scan, and concurrency race conditions
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Security and performance audit on /paypal/subscriptions and /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/status-stream identified several vulnerabilities and stability risks:

  1. Worker Starvation (DoS Risk): SSE stream holds a synchronous PHP worker process for up to 60 seconds with per-second blocking loop.
  2. SQL Wildcard & Cross-Tenant Leak: GetSubscriptionStatusStream performs note LIKE "%{$subscriptionId}%" without input format validation, allowing wildcard % inputs to match arbitrary completed transactions and triggering 1-second interval Full Table Scans.
  3. Upgrade/Downgrade Race Condition: Lack of atomic mutex lock during concurrent upgrade/downgrade requests allows duplicate PayPal subscription creation with duplicated proration discounts.
  4. Auth User ID Extraction: CreateSubscription inspects $request->input('user_id') before $request->user_id injected by the auth middleware.

Proposed Changes

  1. GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php:
    • Enforce strict PayPal Subscription ID regex validation (/^I-[A-Z0-9_-]{8,30}$/i), rejecting invalid inputs with HTTP 400 before DB access.
    • Remove per-second LIKE '%...%' Full Table Scan queries from inside the streaming loop; inside loop only check Redis fast cache. Initial DB check uses exact match (profile_id = ?).
  2. CreateSubscription.php:
    • Completely eliminate $request->input('user_id'). Strictly resolve user identity from $request->user_id injected by auth middleware.
    • Add Redis distributed lock (SET NX EX 20) on paypal:lock:sub_action:{userId} during upgrade and downgrade operations.
    • Fallback buildCallbackUrl to safe configured domain instead of untrusted host headers.

Target Project Board

  • Added to Project Board #43 (GoThru API - Development) with status To Do.

Background

During the recent PayPal subscription security and architecture audit, we analyzed the active endpoint consumption between gothru-dashboard:master (frontend) and GoThru-API-New:main (backend).

We identified 20 unused/obsolete endpoints and action classes in the backend. These routes were originally created as general PayPal API wrappers, but:

  1. Neither gothru-dashboard nor any internal service in GoThru-API-New (cron jobs, queue workers, or controllers) ever invokes them.

issues.display_title: Issue #1992: feat(analytics): implement server-side Countly tracking for payment webhooks and lifecycle events
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Migrate terminal payment and financial outcome tracking from the frontend to the backend. In accordance with the "Webhook-First & Server as Single Source of Truth" architecture, financial captures, subscription revisions, and payment denials must be authoritative and tracked directly from gateway webhooks (PayPal & Stripe).

Scope & Objectives

  1. Countly Ingestion Service:

    • Create a dedicated service/client (CountlyService.php) in Laravel using Http::post() targeting Countly's /i ingestion endpoint.
    • Configure environment variables in .env and config/services.php:
      • COUNTLY_HOST (e.g. https://data.gothru.org)
      • COUNTLY_APP_KEY
    • Implement asynchronous/queued event emission or resilient timeout handling to prevent blocking webhook responses.

  2. Instrument Webhook & Lifecycle Handlers:

    • Emit payment_completed:
      • When PayPal PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED or CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED webhook is verified and captured.
      • When Stripe payment intent or charge succeeds.
    • Emit payment_failed:
      • When PayPal PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED webhook is received.
      • When Stripe payment intent / dunning detects failure.
    • Emit subscription_changed & subscription_change_failed:
      • Inside PayPal/Stripe upgrade, downgrade, and plan modification processors.

  3. Privacy & Security Constraints:

    • Maintain strict Zero-PII policy: Do not send credit card numbers, billing addresses, payer emails, or raw database IDs.
    • Send only sanitized metadata: payment_type, payment_provider, plan_code, action, and normalized reason_code.

  4. Testing & Verification:

    • Unit and Feature tests with mocked HTTP client (Http::fake()) verifying Countly payload structure and non-blocking webhook processing.

issues.display_title: Issue #1997: refactor(internal): prune internal virtual tours response to essential properties with thumbnail and overlay status
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Currently, the internal virtual tours provider endpoint (GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours) executes a SELECT * query on the hosted_tours.tours table, returning 35+ columns per item. Most of these fields are internal database scheduling flags and schema artifacts (e.g. 1_cid, goverlay_activate_date, fschedule_deactivate_at, koverlay_active, xml_version, payed_download) that pollute the response payload, leak internal database structures, and lack a direct panorama thumbnail URL required by caller applications (Panorra, Villume) for their asset picker modals.

Proposed Changes

Refactor InternalVirtualTourRepository and response transformation for GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours to strictly filter and map the return data to the agreed essential contract:

  1. Selective Field Extraction:
    Restrict the returned item attributes strictly to:

    • tour_id (int): Tour identifier.
    • tour_key (string): Unique tour key identifier.
    • tour_name (string): Human-readable tour title.
    • lat (string|null): Latitude coordinate.
    • lng (string|null): Longitude coordinate.
    • 1_cid (string): Direct CID key as stored in database.
    • thumbnail (string): CDN thumbnail image URL (https://img.gothru.org/...) resolved from panorama assets, or empty string "" if not available.
    • goverlay_active (string): Google overlay active status flag ("0", "1", "2", "3").
    • foverlay_active (string): Free/hosted overlay active status flag ("0", "1", "2", "3").

  2. Thumbnail Resolution:

    • Resolve thumbnail URLs efficiently in batch for the paginated page (max 20-100 items) using 4_panoramas.thumb_local_path without N+1 overhead.

  3. Prune Internal Schema Fields:

    • Eliminate all extraneous columns: moderation_id, xml_version, cdn, share_key, stats_key, auto_links, whitelable, favicon, matamo, api_key_id, deactivated*, has_json, type, and all overlay scheduling timestamps (*schedule_*_at, *overlay_activate_date).

  4. Search and Status Filtering:

    • Support keyword search via tour_name, tour_key, and 1_cid.
    • Support optional goverlay_active and foverlay_active status filters supporting single values as well as comma-separated multi-values (e.g. 1,2).

  5. Update Tests & Documentation:

    • Update InternalVirtualTourRepositoryTest and GetUserVirtualToursInternalControllerTest asserting the exact allowed response keys, filter parameters, and status validations.
    • Update docs/v2/tours/management/internal-user-virtual-tours.md.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Retain 1_cid key directly from database.
  • thumbnail returns valid CDN image URL or empty string.

issues.display_title: Issue #1960: 🔴 [Security] PayPal webhook: remove signature-verification bypass — fail-closed verify (forged ?test_mode=1 grants free plans)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PayPal webhook signature verification is currently bypassed whenever isTestMode is true — and isTestMode is inferred from client-controlled inputs. This allows a forged webhook to grant any subscription plan to any user without payment.

Vulnerable code

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalWebhookController.php:33-66

$isTestMode = str_contains($certUrl, 'sandbox')
    || (bool) env('PAYPAL_TEST_MODE', false)
    || (bool) $request->query('test_mode');   // client-controlled!

if (!$isValid) {
    if ($isTestMode) {
        Log::warning('[PaypalWebhook] Sandbox mode: bypassing signature verification failure ...');
        // falls through and PROCESSES the event
    } else {
        return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid webhook signature'], 400);
    }
}

Attack chain

  1. Attacker POSTs POST /paypal/webhooks?test_mode=1 with a forged PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED payload, custom: "user_id:777|plan:agencyy", arbitrary amount.
  2. Signature check fails → bypassed because isTestMode=true → handler runs.
  3. user_id is taken from customData['user_id'] with no ownership validation (PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:74).
  4. processFirstPayment() → cc_purchase insert + updateUserData('agencyy', ...) → user 777 gets a premium plan without paying, plus Redis paypal:sub_status:{sid}=active.
  5. Bonus: resolveProductId() amount-fallback is also attacker-controlled (PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:411-426).

Important context (owner-confirmed)

  • Sandbox and live PayPal webhooks are configured to the same endpoint (one deployment, one URL). Runtime credential routing (PAYPAL_URL_TEST vs PAYPAL_URL, PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID_TEST vs PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID — PaypalHelper.php:46-61, PaypalWebhookHelper.php:42) must be kept.
  • paypal-cert-url header is ALSO attacker-controlled, so removing only the query param is insufficient.
  • Webhook flow now applies to all users (migration guard is obsolete) → this is acute, not theoretical.

Proposed fix (fail-closed, compatible with one-endpoint deployment)

Principle: spoofable input may route credentials, but must never gate verification.

  1. Remove $request->query('test_mode') from isTestMode inference.
  2. Remove the sandbox bypass branch entirely: verification failure → 400 always, regardless of mode.
  3. Preferred: dual-verify — attempt verification against PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID (live), on failure retry against PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID_TEST (sandbox); both failing → reject. The webhook id that verifies becomes isTestMode — environment is then a PayPal-attested fact instead of inferred from any spoofable input. (Fallback option: keep cert-url inference strictly for credential routing, verification stays fail-closed.)
  4. Distinguish network failure during verify (retry; existing transid idempotency makes this safe) from invalid signature (reject). Do not fail open on transient errors.
  5. Startup assertion: PAYPAL_URL must be set — paypalRequest() currently falls back to the sandbox URL by default (PaypalHelper.php:55), so a missing env would silently route live flow to sandbox.
  6. Keep PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SKIP_VERIFY for local dev only; log CRITICAL + alert if set outside dev.

Acceptance criteria

  • No code path processes a webhook whose signature verification failed.
  • ?test_mode= query param is not referenced anywhere in isTestMode inference.
  • Sandbox webhook events still verify and process correctly (verify manually in sandbox).
  • Unit test: forged payload with test_mode=1 → 400; forged Paypal-Cert-Url: sandbox header → 400; genuine live event → 200 processed; genuine sandbox event → 200 processed.

issues.display_title: Issue #1961: 🔴 [Security] PayPal webhook binding verification: persist subscription_id → user_id+plan mapping; reject custom claim mismatch
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

The webhook resolves user_id and plan from resource.custom / custom_id without validating that the subscription actually belongs to that user. Combined with the signature-bypass issue (see related issue), a forged payload can grant any plan to any user. Even with fail-closed signature verification, custom claims are never cross-checked — this binding must become a server-side invariant.

Vulnerable code

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:73-120

$customData = $this->parseCustomData($custom);
$userId = (int) ($customData['user_id'] ?? 0);   // attacker-influenceable claim
$plan = $customData['plan'] ?? null;
// Fallback 1: DB by subscription id (recurring_profile)
// Fallback 2: PayPal API + email match
// ... no check that claim matches the subscription's actual owner

Related: plan: $plan ?? 'basic' fail-open default at :177 — unresolved plan silently grants basic regardless of what was paid.

Why user_id is not a sufficient replacement for isTestMode inference (analysis record)

  • Verification ordering: the webhook id + API credentials must be selected before the payload can be trusted; user_id is not available at that point.
  • Chicken-and-egg: resolving the user itself may require PayPal API calls, which require isTestMode.
  • Allowlist drift (hardcoded HelperClass::getStripeTestUserIds(), HelperClass.php:1253-1272) silently drops legitimate sandbox events after list changes.
  • user_id from custom is not authentication — it must be validated against a server-side binding, not used as a trust anchor.

Proposed fix (binding verification — the permanent forge-killer)

  1. On successful subscription creation, persist a durable mapping: subscription_id → {user_id, plan, env} (DB table or persistent Redis; not TTL-cached).
    • Write locations: `CreateSubscription::handleSubscription/handleUpgrade/handleDowngrade/handleBuyStorage``.
  2. In PaymentSaleCompletedHandler (and all webhook handlers), after signature verification:
    • resolve subscription_id → look up binding → userId/plan must come from the binding, not from custom;
    • mismatch between custom claim and binding → reject + alert (possible forgery or data corruption).
  3. Fail-closed on unresolved plan: if plan cannot be resolved from the binding, do not default to 'basic' — store the raw payload to a dead-letter table for manual review and return needs_review.
  4. isUseStripeTestMode($userId) remains only as a post-verification policy/anomaly-alert layer (sandbox event for a non-test user → alert, don't silently skip).

Acceptance criteria

  • A forged PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED whose custom claims an arbitrary user/plan cannot create cc_purchase/cc_logs or modify user_extra_data.
  • Unresolved plan does NOT default to basic; payload lands in dead-letter storage with alert.
  • Renewal events still resolve correctly (binding lookup takes precedence over custom).
  • Phase 1 Zero-DDL architecture handles fast-path binding via Redis Toronto and fallback to DB/PayPal verified APIs.

Implementation & E2E Verification Result (2026-09-26)

1. Implementation (PR #1964, Phase 1 Zero-DDL)

  • Zero-DDL Rework: To avoid lengthy DBA approval cycles for CREATE TABLE, phase 1 uses Redis Toronto fast-path binding + PayPal-verified resolution (no new DB tables, backfill command removed).
  • Fast-path Binding: Persisted at CreateSubscription into Redis Toronto (paypal:binding:{subscription_id}, ~400-day TTL).
  • Resolution Order: (1) Redis binding fast path -> (2) user_extra_data.recurring_profile DB lookup -> (3) PayPal-verified getSubscriptionDetails.
  • Fail-Closed Resolution: Eliminated default 'basic' plan. Unresolved user/plan logs ERROR and writes a dead-letter record to Redis Toronto (paypal:needs_review:{event_id}, 30-day TTL) while returning benign {status: needs_review} to prevent PayPal retry storms.

2. Production E2E Verification (muhamad.rifky.dev@gmail.com / User 50214)

  • User reset via POST /test-reset-subscription -> verified DB users.subscribtion = 0, user_extra_data cleared.
  • User initiated Basic Plan subscription via Frontend (I-0SH6452H85TT):
    • Redis binding key paypal:binding:I-0SH6452H85TT verified in Redis Toronto:
      {"user_id":50214,"plan":"basic","product_name":"basic","env":"sandbox","action":"subscribe"}
    • Webhook PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED received: resolved user_id: 50214, plan: basic, product_id: 14, sale 0AE65197U6617270J.
    • Database verification on live DB (192.168.1.53):
      • gothru_mod.users: subscribtion = 2 (Basic Plan active).
      • gothru_mod.user_extra_data: recurring_profile = 'I-0SH6452H85TT', current_recurring_plan = 'basic'.
      • ccdb.cc_purchase: record id 165087 inserted with amount $15, product 14, transid 0AE65197U6617270J.

issues.display_title: Issue #1962: 🟠 [Security] PaymentSaleDeniedHandler: forged DENIED/REVERSED events poison Redis + cc_logs (payment UI DoS)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PaymentSaleDeniedHandler has no signature-bypass awareness, no ownership validation, and no rate limiting. Because the webhook endpoint is public and (per the signature-bypass issue) fails open in test mode, a forged PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED / PAYMENT.SALE.REVERSED / BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.PAYMENT.FAILED event can:

  1. Insert attacker-controlled rows into cc_logs_paypal for any user.
  2. Set Redis paypal:sub_status:{sid} to failed with TTL 3600 (PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php:81) — the SSE status-stream then pushes failed to the buyer's browser (GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php:41), flipping a legitimate payment UI to "Payment denied" for up to 1 hour.

This is a direct denial-of-service on real payments and log poisoning. Note: the migration guard (isUseStripeTestMode) exists only in PaymentSaleCompletedHandler — this handler has zero validation.

Vulnerable code

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php:26-94

  • $userId resolved from attacker-controlled custom regex (:37-39)
  • No check that subscription_id actually exists/belongs to the user
  • Unconditional ccLogClass->AddEntryPayPalLink() + redis->setex(... 'failed' ...) (:53-85)

Proposed fix

  1. After the signature verification fix (fail-closed), forged events are rejected at the door — this issue is the defense-in-depth layer:
  2. Validate that subscription_id exists in user_extra_data (recurring_profile / recurring_profile_photo_studio) or in the subscription binding map; unknown subscription → log & ignore (no Redis write, no cc_logs row).
  3. Never write Redis failed from an event whose subscription cannot be bound to a user.
  4. Optional: compare event timestamp vs existing Redis entry before overwrite (prevent stale failed overwriting a fresher active — currently last-write-wins, see cacheStatus() in PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:446-464).
  5. Rate-limit / alert on repeated DENIED events for the same subscription id.

Acceptance criteria

  • Forged DENIED event for a non-existent/unbound subscription id → no Redis write, no cc_logs row.
  • Genuine sandbox DENIED events still reach Redis for the SSE stream.
  • Stale-event overwrite protection implemented (timestamp comparison).

Implementation & E2E Verification Result (2026-09-26)

1. Implementation (PR #1964)

  • Hardened PaymentSaleDeniedHandler:
    • Requires subscription resolution via binding or user_extra_data; unresolvable subscriptions are ignored with zero side-effects (no Redis write, no cc_logs_paypal poisoning).
    • Stale-event overwrite protection: compares event timestamp against existing Redis cache timestamp to prevent old failures overwriting newer active states.
    • Rate limiting: max 5 failure writes per subscription per hour before writes halt.
    • Dead-letter logging: unresolvable denied events record to Redis Toronto (paypal:needs_review:{event_id}, 30-day TTL).

2. Production E2E Verification

  • Tested SSE status stream response against Redis cached states:
    • Cache populated with failed status -> stream immediately pushed:
      {"status":"failed","is_active":false,"message":"Card declined by issuing bank","error_code":"PAYMENT_DENIED"}
    • Prevents frontend endless loading / spinner hang.
  • Verified timestamp comparison logic prevents race conditions between out-of-order COMPLETED and DENIED webhooks.

issues.display_title: Issue #1963: 🟡 Retire obsolete migration guard PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS (webhook-first is now all-users)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php contains a migration guard:

if (!$this->helperClass->isUseStripeTestMode($userId)) {
    if (!env('PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS', false)) {
        Log::info('[PaypalWebhook] Skipped for non-test user (migration guard active)', [
            'user_id' => $userId,
            'plan' => $plan,
        ]);
        return ['status' => 'skipped', 'reason' => 'migration_guard_active', 'user_id' => $userId];
    }
}

This was created when PayPal webhooks were experimental. Per project confirmation: webhook flow is now active for all users in production (PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS=true has been live). Keeping this guard creates dead code, risk of accidental re-enabling if env is misconfigured on new servers, and confuses security reasoning.

Work required

  1. Remove PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS env check.
  2. Invert the relationship: instead of gating processing, use isUseStripeTestMode strictly as a policy check / anomaly alert:
    • if isTestMode === true (verified against sandbox webhook id) AND $userId is NOT in the test user list (!isUseStripeTestMode($userId)):
      • Log CRITICAL: potential misconfiguration or test transaction against a production user.

{

issues.display_title: Issue #1876: feat(schema): add crm_clients table and crm_client_id column on 0_moderation
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

DB schema change required by the CRM dashboard feature (FE branch design/add-CRM-section-menu, design doc: docs/crm/CRM_API_DESIGN.md). No CRM/clients tables exist in any database (audited 2026-09-15 across gothru_mod, moderation, ccdb, hosted_tours, gothru_download_q, 360directory, best360viewer — only match was gothru_mod.oauth_clients, which is unrelated). Executed manually by the operator — no migration code in this repo (database/migrations is intentionally kept empty per project convention).

SQL

CREATE TABLE `moderation`.`crm_clients` (
    `id`          BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    `user_id`     INT UNSIGNED    NOT NULL COMMENT 'Owner — gothru_mod.users.user_id',
    `first_name`  VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'Required (FE)',
    `last_name`   VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    `company`     VARCHAR(200)    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    `email`       VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'Required (FE), indexed, NOT unique',
    `phone`       VARCHAR(50)     NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    `created_at`  TIMESTAMP       NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    `updated_at`  TIMESTAMP       NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
    KEY `idx_crm_clients_user_id` (`user_id`),
    KEY `idx_crm_clients_email` (`email`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB
  DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4
  COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
  COMMENT='CRM client directory, per-user/agency (owner scoping via user_id)';

ALTER TABLE `moderation`.`0_moderation`
    ADD COLUMN `crm_client_id` INT UNSIGNED NULL DEFAULT NULL AFTER `business_name`,
    ADD INDEX `idx_0_moderation_crm_client_id` (`crm_client_id`);

Notes

  • Core relation: 1 tour (0_moderation) ↔ 1 client; 1 client can have many tours (feeds the "Tours Count" column on the CRM page).
  • Table lives in the moderation DB — same MySQL server as 0_moderation so joins are local; connection moderation is already registered for both DEV and LIVE in config/database.php.
  • No FK constraint on the legacy 0_moderation table (huge legacy table, risky ALTER) — unlink is done app-level inside a transaction by the DELETE endpoint (task for DELETE /v1/crm/clients/{id}).
  • email indexed but not unique — FE does not enforce uniqueness.
  • utf8mb4 — client names/company can contain non-latin characters (FE seed data: Tomás Novák, etc.).
  • crm_client_id is nullable → safe for existing rows (all NULL), NULL = tour without client.

Acceptance criteria

  • crm_clients table exists on moderation DB (DEV & LIVE) with utf8mb4 charset
  • 0_moderation has nullable crm_client_id column + index
  • Existing rows unaffected (all crm_client_id NULL)

    • Status: EXISTS
    • Engine: InnoDB, Charset: utf8mb4, Collation: utf8mb4_unicode_ci

    • Indexes: idx_crm_clients_user_id (user_id), idx_crm_clients_email (email)

Request

GET /v1/crm/clients?search=&page=1&limit=10
Param Default Notes
search '' matches first_name / last_name / company / email (LIKE %..%) — parallel to FE filter (name, company, email)
page 1 min 1
limit 10 FE PAGE_SIZE = 10; clamp 1–100

Response (encrypted envelope)

{
  "pagination": { "total_data": 12, "limit": 10, "page": 1, "total_page": 2 },
  "list_clients": [
    { "id": 1001, "first_name": "Olivia", "last_name": "Bennett",

      "phone": "+1 415 555 0142", "tours_count": 3 }
  ],
  "messages": "Data retrieved"
}

tours_count per client:

SELECT c.id, ..., COALESCE(t.tours_count, 0) AS tours_count
FROM crm_clients c
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT crm_client_id, COUNT(*) AS tours_count
    FROM 0_moderation
    WHERE user_id = :user_id AND crm_client_id IS NOT NULL AND delete_space = '0'
    GROUP BY crm_client_id
) t ON t.crm_client_id = c.id
WHERE c.user_id = :user_id ...
ORDER BY c.id DESC
LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset;

Requirements

  • Owner-scoped: every query WHERE user_id = $request->user_id (from auth middleware).
  • SQL isolated in CrmRepository only; flow Controller → Validator → Action → DTO → Repository per ARCH_RULES.md.
  • client object shape identical to FE mock (first_name, last_name, company, email, phone) so the FE swap only touches src/mocks/crm.js.
  • Encrypted envelope via ResponseEnvelopeHelper::encryptResult() (default encrypted, plain via enc flag).

issues.display_title: Issue #1880: feat(crm): DELETE /v1/crm/clients/{id} — delete client & unlink tours
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

New ADR-Domain endpoint DELETE /v1/crm/clients/{id} — hard-delete a CRM client and unlink it from every tour that references it (mirrors mock deleteClient() behavior; FE shows "unlinked from N tours" text in the confirm modal). Design doc: docs/crm/CRM_API_DESIGN.md §4.4.

Behavior — single transaction

No FK constraint exists on 0_moderation.crm_client_id (deliberate), so unlink is app-level:

START TRANSACTION;
UPDATE 0_moderation SET crm_client_id = NULL
WHERE crm_client_id = :client_id AND user_id = :user_id;
DELETE FROM crm_clients WHERE id = :client_id AND user_id = :user_id;
COMMIT;

Response (200)

{ "unlinked_tours": 3, "messages": "Success delete" }

unlinked_tours = affected rows of the UPDATE (consumed by FE t_delete.t_unlink copy).

Errors

domainCode HTTP Condition
CRM.CLIENT_NOT_FOUND 404 DELETE affected 0 rows (not found / not owned)
  • Ownership scoped by user_id (auth middleware).
  • Transaction atomicity: unlink and delete must commit or roll back together.
  • SQL isolated in CrmRepository.

Acceptance criteria

  • Client deleted, all 0_moderation.crm_client_id references set to NULL
  • unlinked_tours reported correctly
  • 404 on missing/not-owned client

Dependencies

  • Schema: #1876 (crm_clients + crm_client_id)

issues.main_description_html: Description: Fix unhandled server errors when sub-agent accounts attempt to generate videos, and implement clean authorization guards preventing unauthorized video creation for sub-agents (reported for user_id: 56439). Currently, generating a 360 Video throws a generic "Invalid input" error, while Walkthrough Video crashes with a PHP fatal error: "count(): Argument #1 ($value) must be of type Countable|array, int given". ## Result & Resolution: Resolved via PR #1919 (Merged). ### 1. Root Causes & Fixes: 1. 360 Video (POST /upload/360v-create): - Cause: time_per_slide and bg_music were marked as required in Create360Video.php. The frontend (gothru-dashboard) sends time_per_slide: null by default, triggering an immediate 409 Invalid input. - Fix: Rules relaxed to nullable with type constraints (integer|min:0 for music, numeric for slide time) and normalized to integers with default fallback (4s / music 0). 2. Walkthrough Video (POST /walkthrough/project & POST /v1/walkthrough/project): - Cause: VideoAppClass::getPaymentStatus() called count($toursSubagent) on an integer count returned by getPublishedMonthlyVideo(). In PHP 8, this caused a fatal error: TypeError: count(): Argument #1 ($value) must be of type Countable|array, int given when sub-agent accounts (like 56439) tried to create videos. - Fix: Fixed accumulation to $total += $toursSubagent;, removed premature returns on non-subagent branch, and corrected $aPost['time_per_slide'] = 8 to $nrSeconds = 8;. ### 2. issues.display_title: Issue #1933: Provide Detailed Destination Storage Error on Transfer Tour Failure
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Provide detailed and professional destination storage error reporting on POST /v2/tours/transfer-overlay when the recipient account lacks sufficient storage, replacing the generic Storage is full. error.

Requirements

  1. Storage Calculation: Compute target user's available space (available_space in GB) and required tour space (required_space in GB).
  2. Detailed Message: Include destination email, available space, and required space in the error message.
  3. Localization: Add messages.tours.transfer_storage_full across all 18 dashboard languages.
  4. Response Contract (409 Conflict):
{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "messages": "Insufficient storage on the destination account. User target@example.com currently has 0.5 GB available, but this transfer requires at least 1.2 GB. Please ensure the recipient has sufficient storage before retrying.",
    "reason": "storage_full",
    "details": {
      "user": "target@example.com",
      "available_space": 0.5,
      "required_space": 1.2
    }
  }
}

issues.display_title: Issue #1936: Implement PayPal Subscription Webhook Ingestion & Status Check API
issues.main_description_html:
Objective

Implement a server-to-server PayPal Webhook listener as the sole authority for subscription payment ingestion into cc_purchase, cc_logs_paypal, user tier activation, and invoice generation, resolving payment loss caused by browser capture disconnects (closes #1934).

Implementation Requirements

1. Metadata Binding (custom_id)

  • In app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/CreateSubscription.php:
    • Attach custom_id = "user_id:{userId}|plan:{plan}|action:{action}" to the subscription creation payload sent to PayPal REST API.
    • Ensures webhook events carry deterministic user and plan context without depending on client-side state.

2. Signature Verification

  • In app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Paypal/PaypalWebhookHelper.php:
    • Call PayPal official API POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature to validate:
      • auth_algo
      • cert_url
      • transmission_id
      • transmission_sig
      • transmission_time
      • webhook_id
    • Reject invalid signatures with HTTP 400.

3. Webhook Listener & Routing

  • Route: POST /paypal/webhooks (public, no auth middleware).
  • Controller: app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalWebhookController.php.
  • Event Handlers in app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/:
    • PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED:
      • Idempotency: verify transaction not already in cc_purchase.
      • First Payment: Insert cc_purchase (note = "First Payment for: {user_id}"), insert 2 entries in cc_logs (S and R), update user tier, call handleAffiliation(), and generate invoice PDF.
      • Recurring Renewal: Insert cc_purchase (note = "Recurring Payment for: {user_id} ({sub_id})"), insert cc_logs_paypal, update expiry, send invoice email.
      • Cache status in Redis: paypal:sub_status:{subscriptionId} {"status": "active", ...} (TTL 1h).
    • PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED & failures:
      • Log failure to cc_logs_paypal with result: 1.
      • Cache failure reason in Redis: {"status": "failed", "error_code": "DENIED", ...}.
    • BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.ACTIVATED / CANCELLED:
      • Sync user_extra_data.recurring_profile and unsubscribes table.

4. Real-time Status Check Endpoint

  • Route: GET /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/status (with auth middleware).
  • Handler: app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/GetSubscriptionStatus.php.
  • Fast response (<5ms) reading from Redis with DB fallback.

5. Rollout Guard

  • Guard webhook processing to test mode / test users (isUseStripeTestMode) during rollout.

Linked Pull Request

  • PR: #1935

Result

  • PR Status: Merged into main via PR #1935.
  • Implemented Components:
    1. CreateSubscription.php: Bound metadata custom_id containing user_id, plan, and action.
    2. PaypalWebhookHelper.php: Cryptographic signature verification via PayPal API /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature.
    3. PaypalWebhookController.php: Automatic Sandbox vs Live environment detection from paypal-cert-url header.
    4. PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php: Deterministic First Payment vs Recurring Renewal separation, idempotency check on cc_purchase.transid, user tier update, affiliation trigger, invoice PDF generation, and Redis status caching (paypal:sub_status:{id}).
    5. PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php: Catches payment failures, logs to cc_logs_paypal, and sets status = failed in Redis with specific PayPal error reason.
    6. SubscriptionActivatedHandler.php & SubscriptionCancelledHandler.php: Automatic subscription profile synchronization.
    7. GetSubscriptionStatus.php: Real-time status polling endpoint (GET /paypal/subscriptions/{id}/status) responding in <5ms from Redis cache with DB fallback.
    8. routes/paypalRoutes.php: Registered public POST /paypal/webhooks and authenticated GET /paypal/subscriptions/{id}/status.
  • Testing & Verification:
    • PaypalWebhookTest.php: 8/8 tests passing (100%).
    • Full PayPal controller test suite (tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/): 48/48 tests passing (100%).
    • Live PayPal Sandbox webhook listener registered and active (01957627G25543502) pointing to https://apil.gothru.co/paypal/webhooks.

issues.display_title: Issue #2002: feat(internal): add endpoint to get virtual tour panoramas by tour key
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Consumer applications (such as Panorra, Villume, and internal GoThru tools) require an internal service-to-service endpoint to retrieve the list of panoramas for a specific virtual tour using its tour_key and authenticated Keycloak user UUID (sub).

Endpoint Specification

  • Method & Path: GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours/{tour_key}/panoramas
  • Auth: keycloak-service-auth:gothru.tours.read (Keycloak RS256 token verification with caller allowlist)
  • Path Parameters:
    • uuid (required, string): RFC 4122 Keycloak user UUID (sub).
    • tour_key (required, string): Hosted tour unique key identifier.
  • Query Parameters:
    • page (optional, int, default: 1): Page number (min: 1).
    • per_page (optional, int, default: 20): Records per page (min: 1, max: 100).

Response Payload (200 OK)

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 128456,
      "sequence": 1,
      "name": "PANO_0001.jpg",
      "lat": "-7.942493",
      "lng": "112.953012",
      "altitude": 0
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "total": 1,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total_pages": 1
  }
}

Field Mapping & Sanitization

  • id: mapped from moderation.4_panoramas.Id (int)
  • sequence: mapped from moderation.4_panoramas.sequence (int)
  • name: mapped from moderation.4_panoramas.1_pano_name (string)

  • lng: mapped from moderation.4_panoramas.3_lng (string/null)

Description

Investigate and resolve HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when requesting the blueline status endpoint:
GET /sv/blueline/{moderation_id}/status (specifically reported on moderation ID 3382231).

Context & Suspected Cause

  1. Route: routes/svpublisherRoutes.php:22 (/blueline/{moderation_id}/status) handled by Tours\GetBluelineStatusController.
  2. Action: App\Actions\Tours\GetBluelineStatusAction executes StreetViewPublisherService::getBluelineStatus($moderationId).
  3. Error handling:
    • If the upstream service (StreetViewPublisherService) returns an unexpected status code (non-200) or error response format that does not match known text branches (no blue line sequence recorded..., sequence_id missing...), the action throws BluelineStatusFailedException.
    • ToursExceptionHttpMapper maps BluelineStatusFailedException (TOURS.SV_BLUELINE_STATUS_FAILED) directly to HTTP 500.

{

issues.display_title: Issue #2010: feat(internal): add endpoint to get virtual tour panorama links by tour key
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Consumer applications (such as Panorra, Villume, and internal GoThru tools) require an internal service-to-service endpoint to retrieve panorama link polylines (connections) for a specific virtual tour using its tour_key and authenticated Keycloak user UUID (sub), mirroring the behavior of /v2/panoramas/links.

Endpoint Specification

  • Method & Path: GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours/{tour_key}/links
  • Auth: keycloak-service-auth:gothru.tours.read (Keycloak RS256 token verification with caller allowlist)
  • Path Parameters:
    • uuid (required, string): RFC 4122 Keycloak user UUID (sub).
    • tour_key (required, string): Hosted tour unique key identifier.
  • Query Parameters:
    • level_id (optional, string): Filter connections by specific floor level / folder ID (replaces fid from v2).

Response Payload (200 OK)

{
  "data": [
    [
      ["112.953012", "-7.942493"],
      ["112.953080", "-7.942510"]
    ]
  ]
}

Behavior & Business Logic

  1. Validate {uuid} against RFC 4122 UUID syntax regex.
  2. Validate {tour_key} is non-empty.
  3. Resolve user via Keycloak sub with atomic JIT provisioning.
  4. Verify tour exists and is owned by the user in hosted_tours.tours (deactivated = '0').
  5. Resolve moderation_id from tour.
  6. Retrieve polyline coordinates using ConstellationClass::getConstellationPolylinesV1($moderationId, $levelId).
  7. Return unencrypted JSON response { "data": [...] }.

Error Responses

  • 400 Bad Request: malformed UUID or empty tour_key
  • 401 Unauthorized: missing/invalid Keycloak Bearer token
  • 403 Forbidden: missing gothru.tours.read permission or untrusted client ID
  • 404 Not Found: virtual tour not found or not owned by user
  • 500 Internal Server Error: unhandled database or server exception

Tasks & Acceptance Criteria

  • Create GetVirtualTourLinksInternalController with RFC 4122 UUID check, tour_key check, and level_id query extraction.
  • Implement getLinksByTourKey in InternalVirtualTourRepository calling ConstellationClass::getConstellationPolylinesV1.
  • Update documentation in docs/v2/tours/management/internal-user-virtual-tours.md and index in docs/v2/tours/management/README.md and docs/REGISTERED_APIS.md.

issues.display_title: Issue #1993: refactor(paypal): clean up dead capture branches and close APPROVAL_PENDING payment bypass in CaptureSubscription
issues.main_description_html:
Background

In gothru-dashboard, all recurring PayPal subscription flows (SUBSCRIBE, UPGRADE, DOWNGRADE, and BUY-STORAGE) have been migrated to the webhook-first architecture (UpgradeIntentProcessor, DowngradeIntentProcessor, BuyStorageIntentProcessor), where DB updates are finalized via webhook events and the frontend listens to the SSE status stream (/paypal/subscriptions/{id}/status-stream).

Frontend client-side capture (POST /paypal/subscriptions/capture) is now exclusively invoked when a user has a one-time subscription profile (one_time_payment === true).

However, the backend CaptureSubscription and its action handlers retain legacy dead branches that accept recurring subscription IDs with APPROVAL_PENDING or APPROVED statuses before actual payment capture. This introduces a critical vulnerability where an attacker can manually call POST /paypal/subscriptions/capture with an uncaptured subscription ID and receive an upgraded tier without paying.

Scope of Work

1. Remove Dead Recurring Branch & Close Payment Bypass in SubscribeHandler.php

  • Enforce that client-side capture is strictly dedicated to one-time payment orders (one_time_payment == 1).
  • For recurring subscriptions (one_time_payment == 0), reject client-initiated capture requests or require verified active status with real payment transactions. Reject any APPROVAL_PENDING status.
  • Ensure that recurring tier provisioning strictly occurs via verified webhook events.

2. Harden CaptureSubscription.php

  • In validateSubscriptionStatus(), remove tolerance for APPROVAL_PENDING and APPROVED. Only allow ACTIVE.
  • Require verified captured payment before executing database updates.
  • Remove dead/unused helper methods (e.g., extractPaymentDataFromSubscription()).

3. Harden Fallback Handlers (UpgradeHandler.php, BuyStorageHandler.php, DowngradeHandler.php)

  • In validateNewSubscriptionStatus(), eliminate APPROVAL_PENDING and APPROVED from allowed statuses (['ACTIVE'] only).
  • Ensure idempotency guards only resolve when the webhook has already finalized the transaction or when the subscription is verifiably active.

4. Unit Testing & Verification

  • Add regression tests verifying that:
    • Any capture request with status APPROVAL_PENDING or uncompleted payment throws HTTP 400.
    • One-time payment (one_time_payment == 1) continues to capture PayPal Orders and provision correctly.
    • Existing webhook intent processors and SSE streams remain unaffected.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Direct call to POST /paypal/subscriptions/capture with APPROVAL_PENDING subscription ID is rejected with HTTP 400.
  • Legitimate one-time payment captures proceed smoothly.
  • Dead branches and unused methods in CaptureSubscription are eliminated.
  • 100% test pass rate across PayPal test suites.

Result

Pull Request

  • PR: #1995
  • Branch: refactor/harden-paypal-capture-subscription-1993
  • Key Commit: fd0a596ad

Key Files Changed

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/SubscribeHandler.php: Enforced one_time_payment == 1 only, rejected recurring subscriptions client-side with 400, removed dead recurring refund/cancel code.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/CaptureSubscription.php: Enforced ACTIVE status only in validateSubscriptionStatus(), removed dead methods extractPaymentDataFromSubscription() and extractPaymentDataFromOrder().
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/UpgradeHandler.php: Enforced ACTIVE only in validateNewSubscriptionStatus().
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/BuyStorageHandler.php: Enforced ACTIVE only in validateNewSubscriptionStatus().
  • resources/lang/*/messages.php: Updated subscription_invalid_state across 18 languages to expect ACTIVE.
  • tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalSubscriptionHardeningTest.php: Added comprehensive regression test coverage.

issues.display_title: Issue #2021: Use real daily Countly time-series data instead of synthetic distribution in Support Analytics
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Replace the synthetic average/sine-wave time-series generation in CountlyReadService::buildTimeSeries with actual day-by-day counts parsed directly from Countly API's event and session trees.

Problem Statement

Currently, CountlyReadService::buildTimeSeries calculates the average daily count across the selected date range (total / daysCount) and applies an artificial sine wave variance (sin($i * 0.8) * 0.15).
As a result:

  • On days with 0 events (e.g. October 7, 2026 for payment_completed), the chart still displays 9 payments.
  • Discrepancies exist between Countly's official dashboard (which shows real day-by-day counts, 0 on Oct 7) and GoThru's Support Analytics chart.

Scope of Changes

  • In app/Services/Analytics/CountlyReadService.php:
    • Retain the raw event and session JSON trees returned by Countly.
    • Implement daily breakdown extraction for each date (YYYY-MM-DD) within the requested range directly from the Countly tree (year -> month -> day -> c, and t/u/n for sessions).
    • Populate each entry in time_series with exact counts for payments_completed, payments_failed, tours_created, users, sessions, and new_users (defaulting to 0 when no data exists for a day).
    • Update CountlyReadServiceTest.php unit tests to use dynamic Carbon dates (e.g. Carbon::setTestNow(...) or current day) and assert exact daily time-series values.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Time-series values match Countly's actual daily counts (e.g., Oct 7 returns 0 if Countly recorded 0).
  • Dates without activity return 0 instead of synthetic estimates.
  • All unit tests pass cleanly with 100% assertions.

Result

Description

An audit of payment telemetry and database records (referenced in #2023) revealed that background recurring renewal cronjobs and dunning retries can severely pollute Countly telemetry with "retry storms". For example, a single customer with a declined recurring card payment can trigger 5 to 8 repeated failures across several days, which distorts the real-time commercial checkout conversion funnel.

In accordance with the agreed telemetry policy, Countly commercial telemetry (payment_failed, payment_completed) must exclusively track user-initiated interactive checkout events. Headless recurring renewal invoices and dunning cycles are already tracked in authoritative ledger tables (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe, ccdb.cc_logs_paypal) and must not emit events to Countly.

Objectives

  1. Remove Countly payment_failed event emission from headless background dunning cronjob (StripeFailedPaymentDetector.php).
  2. Prevent recurring subscription denied webhook events (PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED / BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.PAYMENT.FAILED) in PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php from emitting payment_failed if they are tied to existing recurring subscription billing cycles.
  3. Update existing unit tests (PaymentWebhookCountlyTrackingTest.php, StripeFailedPaymentDetectorTest.php) to assert that recurring background cycles do not emit telemetry events.

Scope of Changes

  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/StripeFailedPaymentDetector.php
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php
  • Unit tests under tests/Unit/

Result

  • Pull Request: #2025 (Merged)
  • Key Commit: 603894de1
  • Verification Evidence:
    • PaymentWebhookCountlyTrackingTest: 5/5 tests passed (100%).
    • StripeFailedPaymentDetectorTest: 12/12 tests passed (100%).
    • Full payment test suite passing 100%.
